### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b7f29ddfe2390dfa5f2c5fc240be03fb6c4aa761` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ad14498fb03b3286e0b9c447087277efc233487a` — the merge of head `6d0b827cd7246bdb6f691166778768b59d508a44` into base `b7f29ddfe2390dfa5f2c5fc240be03fb6c4aa761`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ad14498fb03b3286e0b9c447087277efc233487a && git checkout ad14498fb03b3286e0b9c447087277efc233487a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b7f29ddfe2390dfa5f2c5fc240be03fb6c4aa761 6d0b827cd7246bdb6f691166778768b59d508a44 && git checkout -B drift-repro b7f29ddfe2390dfa5f2c5fc240be03fb6c4aa761 && git merge --no-ff 6d0b827cd7246bdb6f691166778768b59d508a44

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b7f29ddfe2390dfa5f2c5fc240be03fb6c4aa761
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6d0b827cd7246bdb6f691166778768b59d508a44`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts + packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/auth-gate.ts, packages/services/service-print/src/print-routes.ts, packages/types/src/in-process-session-read.contract.test.ts, .changeset/24196-auth-session-api-declared-fields.md

PR #24220 for card #24196, isolated at-tier review, read-only. The head is a merge of `origin/main` `b7f29ddfe2` into the dev branch; the net diff against that merge base is 4 files, +62/-10, and matches GitHub's PR diff byte for byte (index lines aside). The PR head had not moved past this sha when read. Inputs: the card body and its three comments (triage `6238150376`, claim `6239818388`, dev report `6240499223`), the PR body, file list and diff, the head's check-runs, and the cited code read at the head.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface, one change: `AuthSessionApi.getSession`'s result gains five optional members. Each one judged against the reader named on it, read at the head:

- `user.email: string` — right. Read at `resolve-authz-context.ts:562` onto `ctx.email`.
- `user.authGate: unknown` — right. Read at `:555` as `normalizeAuthGate(sessionData?.user)`; `auth-gate.ts:52` reads `sessionUser?.authGate` and nothing else off the user, then validates `code` against `AuthGateCodeSchema` and fills `message` itself. The card's "auth-gate fields `normalizeAuthGate` reads" is therefore one field, and declaring it unvalidated is exactly how that reader takes it (its parameter is `any`; it also validates non-session input at `:110`). A narrower declared shape would restate the validator's job in the contract.
- `session.id: string` — right. Read at `:559` for the dropped-claim log line, with the row-id-never-token comment intact.
- `session.token: string` — right. Read at `:561` onto `ctx.accessToken`.
- `session.impersonatedBy: string | null` — right. Read at `print-routes.ts:274` by `impersonatorOf`. `null` is a value the row carries: `sys_session.impersonated_by` is `Field.lookup('sys_user', { required: false })` (`platform-objects/src/identity/sys-session.object.ts:235`). A contract return wider than better-auth's own `string | undefined` is sound for the implementer (narrower is assignable to wider), and the reader narrows with `typeof by === 'string'` before use.

Nothing undeclared is read by the two readers, which is the card's other half ("if a field turns out not to be read by any reader, it is not declared", and its converse). Every `sessionData` read in the session arm is at `:549` to `:562`: `user.id`, `session.userId`, `session.activeOrganizationId`, `user` (to `normalizeAuthGate`), `session.id`, `session.token`, `user.email` — all declared, no cast around `sessionData`. The print door reads `sessionRead?.session?.impersonatedBy` alone, and the former `as { session?: { impersonatedBy?: unknown } }` cast is gone.

Accept sets: none move. No Zod schema, no authorable key, no REST route, no runtime branch is touched. All three source hunks are type-only; `impersonatorOf` keeps the same `typeof` and `trim()` branches on the same values, and `resolveCaller` returns the same `session` under the same `credential === 'session'` condition.

Widening only, so every implementer and caller typechecks unchanged: each new member is optional, which plugin-auth's `getApi()` (better-auth's own api) and the `const api: AuthSessionApi = {...}` literal in the types contract test both still satisfy. CI's `Type Check · source gates`, `consumer gates`, `debt ledger` and `workspace` legs are all `success` on the head, which covers the closure the dev typechecked by hand (spec, types, core, service-print, plugin-auth, plugin-sharing, service-datasource, plugin-hono-server).

`@objectstack/core`'s published surface is unchanged: `SessionRead` is a module-local alias (not exported) and `ResolveAuthzInput.getSession` stays what it was: a function of `headers: any` answering a Promise of `any`, or `any`. Right; the option of tightening it is ③ item 1.

`@objectstack/service-print`: `ResolvedCaller.session` and the `getSession` closure go from `unknown` to `SessionRead`, both module-internal. `let sessionRead: SessionRead` is legal before assignment because the declared result is `{...} | undefined`, so the alias includes `undefined`. Right.

Generated artifacts: no `.describe()`, no Zod and no export added or removed, so no api-surface, json-schema, docs or authorable-surface artifact moves; the dev reports `check:generated` exit 0 at `7a60e0e5` and the `Type Check · source gates` leg that carries its reconcile is `success`. The types contract test (`DeclaredInput`, the first parameter type of `getSession`) pins the input only, so the result widening leaves it untouched — right that it needed no change.

The docblock's standing claim, "exactly the fields below that they read", now holds for every read this card names. One position outside this diff still contradicts it: a top-level `activeOrganizationId` fallback, confirmed on the head at `service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts:1176` (`session?.session?.activeOrganizationId ?? session?.activeOrganizationId`) and named by the dev at `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3352`. Out of this diff, escalated in ③ item 5.

Gate verdicts on the head, read off the check-runs (theirs, not this record's; this record does not wait on them): `Lint & Repo Gates` success; `Build Core` success; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success (no governed path in the file list); `TypeScript Type Check` success (all four legs, `workspace` included, success); `Check Changeset` success; the card-claim, single-writer and part-of checks success; `Test Core (1/6)` to `(6/6)` still `in_progress` at the time of writing. The queue leg lands only once the required five are `success`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/24196-auth-session-api-declared-fields.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/core: patch`, `@objectstack/service-print: patch`. Matches what the diff publishes: spec widens a published contract's result type, which is `minor` (the floor a `Clause-②: yes` line demands); core and service-print change no exported surface and no runtime behaviour, type-only reader edits in released packages, so `patch` (never `skip-changeset`). Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. The `Clause-②:` line reads `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the changeset and `Clause-②: yes` on the PR body: both are well-formed readings of the one reader (`clause2-line.mjs`: `yes` and `yes (widening)` are the same declaration, the second said out loud), and both are truthful — a declaration widening, no narrowing anywhere in the diff. `Check Changeset` is `success`. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and `open_questions` entry from report `6240499223`:

1. open_question — type `ResolveAuthzInput.getSession` as returning the declared result (B) or leave it `any` (A)? Answered: A, as shipped. B narrows a published `@objectstack/core` input, a `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with an ADR-0087 disposition, inside a card triage graded as a widening; its pull is unmeasured (every closure in the tree returns `api.getSession(...)` or `any`, 15 call sites per the dev). B becomes its own card only on a named external caller or measured drift. The dev's recommendation stands.
2. deviation — the harness attribution reminder versus the model-free trailer pair: checked on the branch's one non-merge commit `7a60e0e5`, which carries the model-free `Claude-Session:` and `Co-authored-by:` pair the rule requires. Resolved.
3. deviation — the PR was not subscribed to CI (os-dev contract): no review consequence; the gate verdicts are read off the head above.
4. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally (exit 3, prerequisite not met): `Lint & Repo Gates` carries it and is `success` on the head. Closed.
5. out_of_scope_finding, "carrier: none, not filed" — the other `getSession` callers still read through `any` or a cast (plugin-auth `:2839` and `:3229` as `(authApi as any)`, the runtime, rest, cloud-connection, webhooks and storage sites the dev lists), and two of them read a top-level `activeOrganizationId` the contract never declared (confirmed at `storage-service-plugin.ts:1176`). Escalated, not blocking: the first half is the contract's own docblock contradicted again — the same class this card was filed as, a contract violation, which Prime Directive 10 wants as a card rather than an acceptance note; the second half is a consumer `??` fallback tolerating an off-contract shape (Prime Directive 12: a declared ADR-0087 conversion or removal, never a bare fallback). This reviewer's one write channel is this comment, so the seat files one follow-up card covering both halves: each remaining reader either reads through the declared type with its field declared for it (`user.role` and `user.isPlatformAdmin` with `judgePlatformAdmin` as the named reader, if that is the direction) or is typed by better-auth's own handle on purpose, and the top-level fallback is converted or removed. Not a FAIL reason here: the dispatch held those callers out of scope ("read to name readers, not edited") and the card's Wanted is met exactly.

No governed path in the file list; the PR is a draft with auto-merge unarmed; the head repository is the base repository, so this is a delivery, not a fork proposal.
